transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the production rollout for the new search-ranking service on Thursday, June 12 at 14:00 UTC, I need to conduct our standard round-robin sign-off with platform engineering, customer support, and security before I can finalize the launch checklist. The service passed staging tests and we're planning to start with 25% of production search traffic. Before I sign off, I need from each of you: any critical dependency findings, and confirmation that your area is clear for production traffic. I also need to lock in the explicit initial traffic percentage and the p99 latency rollback threshold on the checklist. Let's go around the room -- platform engineering first, then customer support, then security. What are you seeing?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical scheduling issue. I confirmed with the account team today that a major enterprise customer's contract requires 48 hours of advance notice for search changes and blocks search changes from 14:00 to 16:00 UTC. Notice was sent Wednesday at 10:00 UTC, so the first compliant launch slot is Friday, June 13, at exactly 16:00 UTC. This has not been added to the launch calendar yet. This means the currently scheduled Thursday June 12 at 14:00 UTC rollout is not compliant with the customer's contract terms.

This is a blocking issue for production launch until the patch is applied.
